cards.statement: For messages published in one region, Pub/Sub ordering preserves publish order within each ordering key.
cards.explanation: An ordering-enabled subscription preserves order among messages sharing a key. Independent keys have independent ordering, so the topic has no single global delivery order.

cards.statement: A Pub/Sub push endpoint acknowledges a message using the HTTP response to the delivery request.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub interprets accepted response statuses as acknowledgment of the pushed message. The endpoint's HTTP response carries the acknowledgment signal.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub makes messages exported to Cloud Storage readable as soon as it appends them to the output object.
cards.explanation: A Pub/Sub Cloud Storage subscription exposes a message batch after Cloud Storage finalizes its object. Appending a message to an open object precedes that visibility.
cards.misconception: Messages become readable immediately after an append to an export object, before object finalization.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub BigQuery subscriptions can calculate windowed totals across messages before inserting table rows.
cards.explanation: Google recommends Dataflow when Pub/Sub ingestion needs windowing or aggregation across messages. BigQuery subscription transforms modify individual messages.
cards.misconception: A BigQuery export subscription performs cross-message windowed aggregation before ingestion.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub push subscriptions can enable exactly-once delivery for subscriber endpoints in a single region.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub's exactly-once delivery feature applies to pull subscriptions, including StreamingPull. Locating a push endpoint in one region does not add support for the feature.
cards.misconception: Using one region makes Pub/Sub's exactly-once delivery feature available to push subscriptions.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub timestamp seeks choose messages using the event timestamp supplied by the source application.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub timestamp seeking uses the publication time recorded by Pub/Sub servers. An application's event time can differ from when its publish request reaches the service.
cards.misconception: Timestamp seeking follows application event time carried in the message.

source.title: Replay and purge messages with seek

cards.statement: Dataflow managed I/O can upgrade connector implementations independently of the pipeline's Apache Beam version.
cards.explanation: Dataflow manages connector versions separately from the Apache Beam SDK. This separation lets a pipeline receive connector fixes while keeping its Beam version.

cards.statement: Dataflow workers with internal IP addresses can reach Google Cloud APIs through Private Google Access.
cards.explanation: Private Google Access provides Google API access for workers using internal IP addresses. Pipeline networking still needs a route and firewall access to those API endpoints.

source.title: Configure internet access and firewall rules

cards.statement: Dataflow streaming jobs with shuffle on worker VMs need firewall rules that permit traffic between workers.
cards.explanation: When worker VMs perform streaming shuffle, they exchange data through the worker VPC. Firewall rules permitting that peer traffic let the job move records between processing stages.

source.title: Configure internet access and firewall rules

cards.statement: The Storage Write API (gRPC) default stream gives each retry an exactly-once write guarantee.
cards.explanation: The Storage Write API (gRPC) default stream uses at-least-once semantics. Exactly-once writes use application-created streams with offsets that identify append positions.
cards.misconception: The default stream deduplicates retries under the Storage Write API (gRPC)'s exactly-once guarantee.

source.title: Introduction to the Storage Write API (gRPC)

cards.statement: In Apache Beam, an event can contribute to separate aggregates in overlapping sliding windows.
cards.explanation: Apache Beam assigns an event to multiple sliding windows when their duration exceeds their start interval. This supports rolling calculations over overlapping event sets.

cards.statement: In Apache Beam, a watermark guarantees that earlier event-time records have finished arriving.
cards.explanation: An Apache Beam watermark estimates event-time completeness based on the data source. A record with an earlier timestamp can still arrive later and count as late data.
cards.misconception: Advancing a watermark proves that the corresponding event-time data is complete.

cards.statement: In Apache Beam, a PCollection carries its allowed-lateness setting into downstream derived PCollections.
cards.explanation: Apache Beam propagates allowed lateness to PCollections derived from the configured collection. A later window configuration explicitly overrides that setting when a different tolerance is needed.

cards.statement: Dataflow Streaming Engine moves window state storage from worker VMs into the Dataflow service backend.
cards.explanation: Streaming Engine keeps window state in managed backend infrastructure. Offloading that state reduces worker disk and memory needs and separates state storage from worker replacement.

source.title: Design for flexibility and efficiency on Dataflow

cards.statement: Dataflow FlexRS keeps regular VMs as standby replacements for preempted workers during batch execution.
cards.explanation: FlexRS runs regular and preemptible VMs together during batch execution. The regular workers contribute alongside preemptible workers rather than waiting as standby replacements.
cards.misconception: FlexRS holds regular workers in reserve until preemptible workers stop.

source.title: Use Flexible Resource Scheduling in Cloud Dataflow

cards.statement: Dataflow's at-least-once streaming mode supports BigQueryIO FILE_LOADS for writing records to BigQuery.
cards.explanation: BigQueryIO FILE_LOADS is incompatible with Dataflow's at-least-once streaming mode. For that mode, use STORAGE_API_AT_LEAST_ONCE as the BigQueryIO write method.
cards.misconception: BigQueryIO file loads work with either Dataflow streaming processing mode.
cards.volatilityNote: Supported BigQueryIO write methods can change as Dataflow streaming modes evolve.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub AI Inference SMT can enrich a message with a model's prediction while retaining the original message data.
cards.explanation: The AI Inference SMT calls a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform model and adds its inference to the Pub/Sub message. Downstream consumers receive the inference alongside the original data.

cards.statement: In Apache Beam, ParDo rejects fixed-window side inputs whose window duration differs from its main input.
cards.explanation: Apache Beam projects a main-input window into the side input's window set. The selected side-input window can have a different duration from the main-input window.
cards.misconception: A fixed-window side input needs the same window duration as the main input.

cards.statement: Cloud Data Fusion uses ephemeral Managed Service for Apache Spark clusters for pipeline runs by default.
cards.explanation: The default Cloud Data Fusion compute profile creates a Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster for a pipeline run and deletes it after completion, keeping the cluster lifecycle tied to that run.

source.title: Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster configuration

cards.statement: BigQuery continuous queries can directly use on-demand compute billing for processing incoming rows.
cards.explanation: BigQuery continuous queries use capacity-based compute. They need an Enterprise or Enterprise Plus reservation with a CONTINUOUS assignment.
cards.misconception: Continuous queries share the on-demand compute option used by ordinary BigQuery queries.
cards.volatilityNote: The reservation and edition requirements for continuous queries may change.

cards.statement: Workflows can wait for an external system's HTTP callback before it starts the next pipeline step.
cards.explanation: A Workflows callback endpoint resumes the waiting execution when it receives a request. This coordinates an external completion event instead of repeatedly polling its status.

cards.statement: Classic Dataflow templates can rebuild their pipeline graph from execution parameters at launch.
cards.explanation: Classic Dataflow templates contain a prebuilt static job graph. Runtime parameters supply values to that graph rather than generate a different graph.
cards.misconception: Classic templates construct a new pipeline graph from launch-time parameters.

cards.statement: A Dataflow Flex Template stores its pipeline container image in Artifact Registry.
cards.explanation: Dataflow pulls a Flex Template's pipeline image from Artifact Registry at launch. The template specification in Cloud Storage points to that image.

cards.statement: Dataflow updates worker-count bounds in place for a running streaming job that uses Streaming Engine.
cards.explanation: For Streaming Engine jobs, Dataflow applies minimum and maximum worker updates while the job keeps running with the same job ID.

cards.statement: For a state-preserving update, Dataflow stops the old job when its compatibility check fails.
cards.explanation: For a state-preserving replacement, Dataflow leaves the old job running if the compatibility check fails. It rejects the incompatible replacement.
cards.misconception: An unsuccessful compatibility check stops the original job during a state-preserving update.

cards.statement: Dataflow supports graph-changing replacement updates for a running batch pipeline.
cards.explanation: Dataflow's pipeline update feature applies to running streaming jobs. Engineers run changed batch pipeline code as another job.
cards.misconception: Dataflow's streaming replacement mechanism also updates running batch pipeline graphs.

cards.statement: Dataform can reach Git repositories in private networks through Developer Connect's proxy.
cards.explanation: Developer Connect's proxy links Dataform to privately hosted Git repositories. Direct HTTPS or SSH connections from Dataform need a public Git endpoint.

source.title: Connect to a third-party Git repository

cards.statement: Dataform release configurations can execute compiled SQL on their compilation schedule.
cards.explanation: A Dataform release configuration's schedule produces compilation results. Workflow configurations schedule execution of those results in BigQuery.
cards.misconception: A scheduled release compilation also executes the compiled SQL workflow.

cards.statement: Dataform uses its default service agent's credentials to run scheduled SQL workflows by default.
cards.explanation: Dataform workflow execution uses a custom service account or user credentials. The default Dataform service agent facilitates execution under the selected identity.
cards.misconception: The default Dataform service agent is the execution identity for scheduled SQL workflows.
cards.volatilityNote: Dataform execution identities and enforced act-as behavior have changed recently.

cards.statement: A configured Cloud Build trigger can automatically invoke a Dataform workflow after a matching Git push.
cards.explanation: Cloud Build triggers enable event-driven Dataform releases. A configured build compiles the pushed code and starts a workflow invocation to update the data.

cards.statement: Bigtable can concentrate sequential writes on one node when row keys begin with timestamps.
cards.explanation: Timestamp prefixes group new writes into a narrow key range, creating a hotspot. A higher-cardinality prefix spreads incoming writes across more of the table.

cards.statement: Bigtable groups rows sharing a row key prefix into a contiguous range for efficient range reads.
cards.explanation: Bigtable sorts row keys lexicographically. A prefix-based key design lets a reader scan matching rows as a range instead of scanning the whole table.

cards.statement: Bigtable Data Boost can process bulk row deletions using compute isolated from the serving cluster.
cards.explanation: Bigtable Data Boost provides separate serverless compute for analytical reads. It rejects write and delete requests, so bulk deletion needs cluster compute.
cards.misconception: Isolated analytical compute also handles bulk mutations.

cards.statement: Spanner can reduce network traffic for primary-key joins by interleaving child tables with their parent.
cards.explanation: Interleaving places related parent and child rows together in storage. Spanner can perform primary-key joins locally when those rows occupy the same split.

cards.statement: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL replaces a table's row store when its columns enter the columnar engine.
cards.explanation: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL keeps row-based access alongside the column store. Its optimizer can select row-store access even after the table's columns load into the columnar engine.
cards.misconception: Loading columnar data converts the table's underlying storage instead of adding an analytical access path.

cards.statement: Firestore Standard edition supports the Firestore with MongoDB compatibility API for database access.
cards.explanation: The Firestore with MongoDB compatibility API is available in Enterprise edition. Standard edition offers Native mode or Datastore mode, so edition choice determines API compatibility.
cards.misconception: MongoDB compatibility is available in both Firestore editions.
cards.volatilityNote: Firestore edition capabilities and supported access modes can change.

cards.statement: BigQuery rewrites stored data into a new format when a dataset switches to physical storage billing.
cards.explanation: BigQuery changes storage metering when a dataset switches billing models. The stored data keeps the same compressed physical format, so the switch leaves query performance unchanged.
cards.misconception: A storage billing model controls the table's physical representation.

cards.statement: BigQuery bills time travel and fail-safe bytes separately when a dataset uses physical storage billing.
cards.explanation: Physical storage billing charges time travel and fail-safe storage at the active storage rate. Retained historical versions therefore contribute to the dataset's storage bill.

cards.statement: BigQuery starts a daily time partition's expiration interval from the first row inserted into that partition.
cards.explanation: BigQuery calculates a daily time partition's expiration from its midnight UTC boundary. A late-arriving row inherits the partition's age rather than starting a new expiration interval.
cards.misconception: A partition's expiration clock starts when data first arrives.

cards.statement: Cloud Storage postpones an eligible lifecycle deletion while an object hold remains active.
cards.explanation: An object hold blocks the lifecycle Delete action. After the hold is removed, Cloud Storage can delete the object if the lifecycle rule's conditions still apply.
